evidence_items.explanation: The gSCAN experiments report substantial failures when neural models must apply compositional rules to unfamiliar combinations. This supports the recurring neural-difficulty part of the claim, but does not establish symbolic superiority across the entire period.

In a comparison of seven models, the meta-trained neural approach combined systematicity and flexibility that the symbolic and ordinary neural comparators did not jointly achieve. This contradicts a stable categorical division between successful symbolic generalization and unsuccessful neural generalization.
